about.title: Union City Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Union City is home to roughly 74,500 people who move through grocery stores, apartment complexes, restaurants and shopping centers along Mission Boulevard, Alvarado Niles Road and Whipple Road every day. Each of those properties comes with a legal duty: the owner or manager must keep the place reasonably safe and either fix known hazards or warn people about them. When they don't, and someone slips, trips or falls, California premises liability law may hold them responsible. The hard part is usually proving what lawyers call notice — that the owner knew, or should have known, about the spill, the loose tile or the missing handrail before you got hurt. That is why what you do in the first days matters so much. Photograph the hazard from several angles, note the time, get names of anyone who saw it, and ask the business in writing to preserve its surveillance footage. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We simply connect Union City residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate the facts and explain your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Union City Residents Use LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Attorneys who understand the notice requirement
items.desc: California generally requires you to show the owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to act. The attorneys in our network know how to look for cleaning logs, inspection schedules and prior complaints that speak to that question.

items.title: Fast action to preserve video
items.desc: Many Union City businesses overwrite security footage within days. Getting an attorney involved early means a preservation letter can go out before the evidence disappears.

items.title: Clear guidance on deadlines and shared fault
items.desc: Most premises claims carry a two-year filing deadline, but the window is much shorter if the property belongs to a public entity. California's pure comparative fault rule also means a claim can still go forward even if you were partly to blame — your recovery is just reduced by your share.

items.question: I fell at a store in Union City but didn't report it that day. Is my claim ruined?
items.answer: Not necessarily, though the sooner you report it the better. Write down exactly what happened while it is fresh, go back and photograph the area if it is safe to do so, and see a doctor so your injuries are documented. An attorney can still request incident reports and surveillance footage, but delays make that footage more likely to have been erased.

items.question: What if I was looking at my phone when I slipped?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means your own carelessness does not automatically end the claim. Instead, any compensation is reduced by the percentage of fault assigned to you. If the owner ignored a hazard for hours, a jury might still place most of the responsibility on them.

items.question: Does it matter whether I fell on city property or private property in Union City?
items.answer: Yes, quite a bit. If you were hurt on a sidewalk, park or building owned by the City of Union City, Alameda County or another public agency, you typically must file a government claim within six months rather than the usual two years. Missing that shorter window can bar the case entirely, so it is worth getting a professional opinion quickly.
